results.title: ATOM hits Marcos’ statements on ill-gotten wealth
results.description: MANILA, Philippines — The August Twenty One Movement (ATOM) on Saturday hit out at President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s denial of ill-gotten wealth involving his family. Marcos said in the luncheon hosted by the Foreign Correspondents Association of the Philippines (Focap) that their family’s assets were “not ill-gotten wealth”, echoing an interview with Australian journalist Sarah Ferguson in 2024, where he apparently stuttered. “But we, the August Twenty-One Movement, vehemently disagree with this claim of Mr. Marcos Jr. This is untrue and absolute fake news! We will not just let this pass without disputing this new claim of his. Which is not really surprising, considering that the Marcos brand has always been known to be associated with lies and propaganda,” the movement said. “Be that as it may, getting to Malacanang does not entitle him to distort Philippine history. Getting to Malacanang should not give anyone, for that matter, the audacity to violate the truth. But what can a man who was born and raised by a family that treats falsehood as their basic need to abuse others do? Well, Bongbong still lies every time he gets the chance because, to him, it is just the way life is. Perhaps the Marcos children simply cannot handle or discern the truth,” they added. ATOM also cited that the President’s mother, former First Lady Imelda Marcos, was sentenced by the Sandiganbayan to prison for 6 to 11 years, for the anti-corruption law when she was found to illegally funnel $200 million to Swiss foundations in the 1970s, while she served as governor of Metro Manila, during her husband’s presidency. The elder Marcos served as Metro Manila governor from 1975 to 1986, following the People Power Revolution. “Many victims of Martial Law rejoiced with this news; she was, after all, the second half of the Conjugal Dictatorship that ruled our country with an iron fist for almost two decades. Unfortunately, until now, we have not heard what happened in that case,” ATOM said. “This shows how powerful the Marcoses and the Romualdezes have been ever since. No one from the dictatorship ever spent a day in jail after 1986. This is why a Marcos copycat rose to power, Rodrigo Duterte,” the movement added. Marcos held a luncheon with Focap on Friday and had a speech at the Diamond Hotel in Manila. “Today, that responsibility has become even more demanding as information, whether true or fabricated, whether AI-generated or deliberately manipulated, can spread instantly across digital platforms,” the President said in his speech. Known for their involvement in the EDSA People Power Revolution in 1986, ATOM was named after the date when opposition leader Benigno Aquino Jr. was assassinated, on Aug. 21, 1983. The 43rd anniversary of Aquino’s assassination will be commemorated on Friday, Aug. 21, 2026.

results.title: Kiprich mourns the death of his father
results.description: Dancehall artiste Kiprich, real name Marlon Plunkett, is in mourning after his father, Magnus Lloyd Plunkett, died suddenly on Friday at age 72. The deejay revealed his father had been battling kidney issues and was due for follow-up urine tests. "My brother is down in Jamaica and he was cooking some soup for him... and when he went to check on him, he was unresponsive," Kiprich said. Plunkett was later pronounced dead at hospital. Affectionately known as "Mr Chin," the elder Plunkett was hailed by his son as a sharp businessman, a fearless transport operator/owner and a selfless mentor. "He was able to turn any small business into something major... his mentorship was unmatched," Kiprich said, adding that his dad was a die-hard reggae lover who danced with a signature "rude boy" swagger. He leaves behind four sons — Kiprich, Ricardo, Sprite Rafer and Jamal Plunkett — and a daughter, Kayla Plunkett, as well as his wife, Carrol Plunkett, to whom he'd been married since 1994. Kiprich has had a tough emotional roller coaster year as he lost his newborn baby sired with his fiancée earlier this year. "This ah one of the roughest years, mi father, only Almighty knows," he said.
